root_idea.summary: Softness and the absence of ruggedness: what is smooth, level, gentle, or easy rather than rough or difficult.
root_idea.development: The concrete contrast between smooth or level ground and rugged ground extends to ease, facilitation, gentleness, leniency, and related derived physical uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural سُهُول is presented under the supported singular dictionary citation form سَهْلٌ.

senses.definition: A smooth, level tract of land; a plain.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural construct سُهُولِهَا, “its plains,” referring to level tracts of land and contrasting with rugged terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become smooth, soft, plain, or level.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a place or thing, in contrast with becoming rugged or hard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become easy or facile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of speech that has smoothness or ease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something smooth, soft, plain, or level.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use applied to a place or other thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something easy or facilitate it; to lighten an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With a way or channel, it can mean preparing a passage for water or other movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A welcoming formula expressing that the visitor has come among kin and to a smooth, easy place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional greeting and welcome expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deal easily, gently, or leniently with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may also describe acting or affecting to act gently toward the other party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To descend to, betake oneself to, or settle in plain or level terrain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of moving from rugged ground to a plain and abiding there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use ease or gentleness in dealing with people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Opposed to dealing with people harshly or roughly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find a thing or place smooth, soft, plain, or level.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use applied to a place, object, or similar thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of medicine, to relax or loosen the bowels; to attenuate a bodily humour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive construction describes a person or belly whose bowels have been relaxed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to bring forth a fetus or offspring prematurely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized obstetrical construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become easy or facilitated, or to experience ease in one's affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of an affair or its means of accomplishment; also of a person who finds ease in his affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act easily, gently, or leniently toward one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal use, synonymous with mutual tolerance or leniency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be negligent or careless in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a later or contemporary usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In language and lexicology, a tolerated looseness or laxity of expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may involve an expression acceptable only in a figurative sense, or mentioning the whole while intending a part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take for oneself an easy place or position of abode.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression meaning that one who lies takes an easy place of abode for himself in Hell.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon or deem something easy or facile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive evaluative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smooth, soft, plain, or level; not rough or rugged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of things or terrain and, substantivized, of what has these qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Easy or facile; readily manageable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a person's disposition, it can mean easy in character or easy to lead; of speech, easy in expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In descriptions of the face or cheeks, having the facial form specified by the expression: little flesh in the face, or expanded cheeks not raised in their balls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use in expressions concerning facial appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crow or raven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use from the adjective and terrain noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a river or land, containing or abounding in coarse sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a river or tract of land having سِهْلَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sea-sand or other coarse, non-fine sand; also sand-like earth brought by water or found in a watercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also be applied to gravel-like coarse material issuing from the bladder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to plain terrain, or growing or pasturing in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective derived from سَهْلٌ or أرض سهلة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A laxative medicine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medicine used to loosen or relax the bowels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Canopus, a well-known star.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is also used in traditional astronomical naming of related stars or star groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proverbial comparison meaning “more lying than the wind,” or referring to a certain liar named Suhaylah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed proverbial expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relaxed or loosened by medicine, especially said of the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested form is مُسْهَلٌ; the alternative مَسْهُولٌ is not accepted without explicit authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A laxative or attenuant medicine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medicine that loosens the bowels or attenuates bodily matter.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Physical change to smoothness or levelness.
Speech smoothness or ease is covered by the easy sense.
Preparing a route or channel for water.
Welcome formula and its conventional interpretation.
Gentle or easy dealing with another.
Moving to and settling in plain terrain.
Finding a thing smooth or level.
Later usage of negligence or carelessness.
Attested specialized use of taking an easy abode.
Physical adjective of smoothness, softness, or levelness.
Substantive noun for a plain or level tract.
River or land containing coarse sand.
Coarse sand and related sand-like material.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural construct سُهُولِهَا, while the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form سَهْلٌ.
سَهْلٌ also has a distinct Classical Arabic lexical use meaning “crow,” which is kept separate from the terrain adjective and noun.
